full_build.setup_command: source ./prepare-build.sh <codename>  — must be sourced, not executed
full_build.memory_requirement: ~2GB RAM per thread — limit with BB_NUMBER_THREADS=n or in build/conf/local.conf
full_build.container_options: Docker (requires sudo) or podman (rootless, no daemon). Both accept nearly identical commands.

sdk.two_versions: ARM-based (for watches, target armv7vehf-neon) and qemux86 (for emulator). Both can coexist on the same machine.
sdk.cmake_workflow: source environment-setup → cmake -B build → cmake --build build

layers.meta-smartwatch: BSP layers per watch codename (meta-catfish, meta-sturgeon etc.)
layers.priority: 7 for most AsteroidOS layers, 5 for general OE layers

devtool_workflow.modify: devtool modify <recipe>  — extracts source to build/workspace/sources/<recipe>
devtool_workflow.finish: devtool finish <recipe> <layer>  — creates patch files and updates recipe in named layer
devtool_workflow.add: devtool add <name> <local-dir>  — auto-creates recipe from local source directory
devtool_workflow.note: devtool workspace does not delete source directory unless explicitly asked

ipk_manual_deploy.note: four ipk variants generated: release, -dbg, -dev, -src. Use the shortest-named one.

new_recipe_depends.wiki_note: wiki always includes asteroid-generate-desktop-native in DEPENDS for all new apps

build_methods.recommended: devtool + bitbake — only method that produces correct .ipk with dependencies
build_methods.command_line: fast to set up, doesn't reliably create .ipk or handle dependencies
build_methods.qtcreator: GUI-friendly but difficult to set up, no .ipk output

debugging.qmltester: asteroid-qmltester app on watch — load QML file directly for rapid iteration
debugging.vim_ssh_edit: vim scp://ceres@192.168.2.15/Prototype.qml — edit QML directly on watch via SSH, test with qmltester
debugging.desktop_qml_tool: qml tool (from Qt) runs QML on desktop — stub out watch-specific features
debugging.gdbserver: mentioned in wiki but not yet documented
debugging.qml_profiling: mentioned in wiki but not yet documented

watchface_creation.tooling: unofficial-watchfaces repo contains ./watchface script for test/clone/deploy
watchface_creation.local_test: qmlscene via qt-creator package — run watchface locally before deploying
watchface_creation.session_restart: deploy script restarts session automatically so new fonts and images load
watchface_creation.image_naming: prefix all asset filenames with watchface name to avoid cross-watchface conflict
watchface_creation.font_licenses: OFL/SIL, Apache, BSD, CC-BY only — must allow embedded redistribution
watchface_creation.svg_minimum_size: SVG width and height must be at least 800x800px — Qt only downscales correctly, not upscales
watchface_creation.sizing_guideline: base major sizing on watch width not height — Beluga is taller than wide so width is the smaller dimension
watchface_creation.background_guideline: do not fully hide the user-selected wallpaper
watchface_creation.thumbnails: square thumbnail on flatmesh background, round thumbnail on developer-chosen background

emulator.qemu_requirement: must be built with Virgil3D support (virtio-vga-gl device)
emulator.run_command: qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -kernel bzImage-emulator.bin -device virtio-vga-gl -net nic -net user,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 -drive format=raw,file=asteroid-image-emulator.rootfs.ext4 -m 512 -display sdl,gl=on -cpu qemu64,+ssse3,+sse4.1,+sse4.2 -usb -device usb-tablet --append 'verbose root=/dev/sda rw mem=512M video=800x800'
known_issues: must run in Wayland session — known problems under X11
NVIDIA proprietary drivers cause black screen or video artifacts — use gtk display backend instead of sdl
click registration offset — resize window taller to improve accuracy
pre-2024-08-11 images: ceres not in input group — fix: usermod -a -G input ceres && systemctl restart user@1000
emulator.demo_mode: ssh -t -p2222 root@localhost mcetool -D on  (prevents screen blanking)

graphic_stack.compositor: asteroid-launcher, based on Lipstick from Nemomobile, built with QML + qml-asteroid
graphic_stack.qpa_compositor: qt5-qpa-hwcomposer → libhardware.so (glibc) → libhybris → Android libhardware.so (bionic) → proprietary GPU blobs
graphic_stack.app_rendering: Qt5 QtWayland client QPA → wayland-egl protocol → asteroid-launcher (Wayland compositor)
graphic_stack.not_qt_only: any app supporting the Wayland protocol can run, not just Qt apps
graphic_stack.libhybris_purpose: bridges glibc and bionic to reuse Android GPU drivers — same approach as SailfishOS, NemoMobile, WebOS-Ports
graphic_stack.note: Graphic Stack page last edited June 2023 — may not reflect details of newer ports like hoki/rubyfish

boot_sequence.chain: bootloader (proprietary, fastboot protocol) → kernel (Android kernel + BT backport) → systemd
boot_sequence.bootloader_access: swipe top-left to bottom-right on screen at boot, or adb reboot bootloader
boot_sequence.kernel_format: boot.img = kernel (+ device tree) + initramdisk. Tools: mkbootimg/unmkbootimg
boot_sequence.boot_partitions: BOOT, RECOVERY, or fastboot boot via USB
boot_sequence.debug_boot: append debug-ramdisk to kernel params (via fastboot --cmdline) to enable adb in ramdisk before systemd
boot_sequence.systemd_logs: stored in tmpfs by default (lost on reboot). To persist: disable /var/volatile mount in /rfs/etc/fstab, mkdir /rfs/var/log/journal

chipsets.msm8226: older SoC — dory, bass, lenok, sturgeon, sparrow, anthias (kernel 3.10)
chipsets.msm8909w: mid-range SoC — catfish, sawfish, narwhal, skipjack, swift, beluga, triggerfish (kernel 3.18–4.9)

key_devices.catfish: TicWatch Pro 2018/20, msm8909w, kernel 3.18, Android pie
key_devices.rubyfish: TicWatch Pro 3, msm8937, kernel 4.9, Android pie
key_devices.hoki: Fossil Gen 6, msm8937, kernel 4.14, Android pie
key_devices.beluga: OPPO Watch, msm8909w, kernel 4.9, Android pie — RECTANGULAR screen (portrait, taller than wide)
key_devices.sturgeon: Huawei Watch, msm8226, kernel 3.10 — used as SDK build target codename

watch_hardware.new_port_in_progress: Google Pixel Watch 3 (seluna/solios), sw5100 chipset, kernel 5.15, Android 16 — listed but no support status

bluetooth.sync_app: AsteroidOSSync on Android — uses SweetBlue library (BLE central)
bluetooth.watch_daemon: asteroid-btsyncd — runs as ceres user, DBus multiplexer between BlueZ5 and apps
bluetooth.bt_chip: BCM20715 (Broadcom) on dory-family devices — needs proprietary firmware via patchram systemd service
bluetooth.bluez_version: BlueZ5 with BT 4.1 backport for MGMT API

media.characteristics: title(7001), album(7002), artist(7003), playing(7004), command(7005), volume(7006 0-100)

notification.format: UTF-8 XML: <insert> with pn/id/an/ai/su/bo/vb children, or <removed> with id

screenshot.format: write any byte to request, content streamed as JPEG chunks

time.format: 6 bytes: year-1900, month(0-11), day, hour, minute, second

weather.format: 5 two-byte big-endian values per characteristic (today + 4 days forecast)

ble_profiles.ancs: Apple Notification Center Service also implemented (UUID: 7905F431-B5CE-4E99-A40F-4B1E122D00D0)

connectivity.rndis_fix: sudo dhclient -v enp0s20f0u8  (if host doesn't auto-get IP)

useful_commands.launch_app: EGL_PLATFORM=wayland QT_QPA_PLATFORM=wayland QT_WAYLAND_DISABLE_WINDOWDECORATION=1 invoker --single-instance --type=qt5 /usr/lib/asteroid-appname  (run as ceres)
useful_commands.screen_demo_mode: mcetool -D on  (keeps screen on — useful during dev)

fastboot_entry.adb_method: adb reboot bootloader  (works when watch is running)
fastboot_entry.catfish_hoki_skipjack: hold both buttons during boot until fastboot menu appears
fastboot_entry.dory_bass_lenok_sparrow_swift_wren: swipe diagonally top-left to bottom-right during first seconds of boot
fastboot_entry.sawfish_sturgeon: hold power button at bootlogo until vibration finishes, release, press again quickly
fastboot_entry.triggerfish_nemo: hold lower button while powering on

package_install.force_depends: opkg install --force-depends packagename.ipk  (use with caution — can cause instability)

bsp_layer_structure.location: src/meta-XXX-hybris/ in the AsteroidOS build tree

base_layer_by_android_version.android_9_pie: base on meta-beluga or meta-triggerfish — check-config script not adapted for Pie, enable SELinux options manually

bsp_layer_structure.machine_conf: conf/machine/XXX.conf — defines screen characteristics, hardware-specific packages
bsp_layer_structure.new_watch_script: meta-smartwatch/scripts/new-watch.sh — clones and renames base layer

kernel_recipe.source: Find vendor kernel at android.googlesource.com/kernel/msm/+refs — set SRC_URI + SRCREV
kernel_recipe.config_check: meta-asteroid/scripts/check-config -w — fixes config values for pre-Oreo kernels
kernel_recipe.boot_image_tools: abootimg, mkboot, or mkbootimg — try all three if one fails silently (watch-specific, no apparent reason)
kernel_recipe.boot_image_format: zImage + initramfs → boot.img. Inherit appropriate bbclass from meta-asteroid/classes/
kernel_recipe.bt_backport_patch: Backport mainline 4.1 BT subsystem — required for MGMT API needed by BlueZ5/asteroid-btsyncd

android_system_dir.purpose: provides Android HALs used by libhybris — only a limited subset of Android libs needed
android_system_dir.reference_build: README-system-dir in meta-dory-hybris — document your own for reproducibility

porting_sequence.display_debug: EGL_PLATFORM=hwcomposer QT_QPA_PLATFORM=hwcomposer asteroid-launcher  (segfault on first run is expected — points to Android graphic HAL issue)
porting_sequence.touch_debug: modify asteroid-launcher start command to use correct evdevtouch /dev/input/eventN
porting_sequence.sensors_test: test_sensors command — 'Operation not permitted' means sensor daemon not started
porting_sequence.audio_test_play: gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=input.mp3 ! mpegaudioparse ! mpg123audiodec ! pulsesink
porting_sequence.audio_test_record: gst-launch-1.0 pulsesrc ! audioconvert ! wavenc ! filesink location=recording.wav
porting_sequence.bt_low_power: bluesleep/Nitrous kernel module needs patch to receive HCI events from kernel BT subsystem instead of /proc/lpm/

debugging.debug_packages: append 'strace gdb asteroid-launcher-dbg' to asteroid-image class temporarily
debugging.last_kmsg: /proc/last_kmsg in WearOS — enable CONFIG_ANDROID_RAM_CONSOLE kernel option
debugging.ramdisk_debug: append debug-ramdisk to kernel params via fastboot --cmdline to get adb shell in ramdisk before systemd

steps: request meta-XXX-hybris repo creation on #Asteroid IRC
send PR to AsteroidOS/asteroid to add machine to prepare-build.sh

documentation_decisions.summary: The For Users section of the wiki was restructured from a flat 13-item list into six named groups: Before you install, Getting started, Using AsteroidOS, Connectivity and sync, Managing your watch, Reference. Porting Status was moved to For Porters. Three new pages were created: Interface Overview, Quick Settings Panel, Settings Reference. __NOTOC__ was added to the Documentation main page to suppress the auto-generated TOC that MediaWiki inserts before the first heading. Horizontal rule dividers (----) were added above each of the three top-level sections (For Users, For Developers, For Porters).

Current For Users wiki page inventory as of 2026-04. New pages: Interface Overview (https://wiki.asteroidos.org/index.php/Interface_Overview), Quick Settings Panel (https://wiki.asteroidos.org/index.php/Quick_Settings_Panel), Settings Reference (https://wiki.asteroidos.org/index.php/Settings_Reference). Existing pages retained unchanged: Quick Start Guide, Applications, Synchronization Clients, SSH, IP Connection, Watchface and Package Installation, Updating AsteroidOS, Backup Guide, Useful Commands, Translating AsteroidOS, Licenses. Notifications and App Launcher were decided not to need dedicated pages — covered within Interface Overview.

The Applications wiki page community section is missing three apps as of 2026-04: asteroid-meteormatch (moWerk), asteroid-beatfork (moWerk), and asteroid-hackwatch (recent addition by another contributor). asteroid-qmltester is listed as a community app but is a developer tool and arguably belongs in the For Developers section or needs a clear developer-only label.

A QR code feature is planned for the watch UI to surface a documentation link so users who flashed from any source can find the user guide without having read any docs beforehand. This was the primary motivation for the For Users restructure — a clean, stable, well-structured entry point into the docs is required before the QR code feature ships.

New wiki page 'Finding a Watch' added to the Getting started group. Covers: secondhand market as primary acquisition channel for out-of-production hardware, preference for intact battery when buying used, visual identification via the Watches page on asteroidos.org, codename identification via fastboot bootloader (manual button combo from Useful Commands page, or following install instructions to the bootloader unlock step). Includes pointer to Matrix chat for flashing issues and link to Quick Start Guide as next step.

Display blanking section added to Interface Overview covering: automatic blanking after ~10s inactivity with AoD fallback; tap-to-extend doubles timeout per tap, 5 consecutive extensions causes indefinite stay-on requiring manual dismissal; some apps (Flashlight, games) block blanking automatically and must be explicitly closed. Manual sleep methods: power button (if available) forces immediate sleep; palm-to-sleep covers ambient light sensor triggering immediate sleep, always active on watches with a light sensor, cannot be disabled.

ADB section appended to the SSH wiki page. Key facts documented: some watches have broken SSH and require ADB as the only shell access method; ADB provides equivalent root shell access to SSH; enabled/disabled in Settings > USB alongside SSH; adb shell gives root shell equivalent to ssh root@192.168.2.15; multiple connected watches listed via 'adb devices'; specific watch targeted with 'adb -s <port> shell'. Wiki listing display text changed to [[SSH|SSH and ADB Access]] while page name kept as SSH to preserve inbound links. Connectivity and sync group reordered: Synchronization Clients first, SSH and ADB Access second, IP Connection third.
